questions.question: Explain what the Group Areas Act did and the real purposes it served.
questions.expected_answer: 1950 Act: government could proclaim areas for one racial group (based on Population Registration Act); others could not own or live there and could be removed; controlled business ownership; amended/reissued 1957, 1966. Built on Natives (Urban Areas) Act 1923; aimed to eliminate mixed areas. Claimed to reduce friction; really protected white property and best land near city centres, removed communities whites wanted, weakened Indian traders, controlled black population with distant townships, buffer zones and few entrances, broke mixed political communities. Used with Natives Resettlement Act 1954, Prevention of Illegal Squatting Act 1951; overwhelmingly black, coloured and Indian people removed.

questions.question: Describe Sophiatown before the removals and explain why the government wanted it removed.
questions.expected_answer: About 6 km west of Johannesburg; Herman Tobiansky bought land 1903, named after wife Sophia; sewage site deterred whites, plots sold to all races. Rare freehold rights for black owners; tenants and backyard rooms, overcrowding; Western Areas (Martindale, Newclare). Poverty and gangs, but vibrant, cosmopolitan Kofifi: jazz, marabi, shebeens (Dolly Rathebe, Hugh Masekela), Drum writers (Can Themba, Bloke Modisane, Henry Nxumalo), Father Trevor Huddleston. Government saw black ownership, racial mixing and political activity as a threat; white neighbours (Westdene) demanded removal of the "black spot".

questions.question: Describe the removal of Sophiatown, the resistance to it, and the legacy of forced removals.
questions.expected_answer: 1953 Western Areas Removal Scheme; Natives Resettlement Act 1954; low compensation, loss of freehold, renting at Meadowlands (Soweto). ANC, TIC campaign, Freedom Square meetings, Mandela and Huddleston; "We won't move", "Ons dak nie, ons phola hier". 9 February 1955, three days early, about 2 000 armed police in rain; resistance called off (force, surprise, no plan, divided community, tenants attracted to houses). Removals into early 1960s; other groups split off; bulldozed; Triomf. Song "Meadowlands". Legacy: District Six (11 Feb 1966, about 60 000 to Cape Flats), Cato Manor, South End, Lady Selborne; about 3.5 million removed 1960-1983; loss of property, community, trauma, long commutes; Act repealed June 1991; Restitution of Land Rights Act 1994; Triomf renamed Sophiatown 2006; museums.
